items.bodyExcerpt:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #9447

`GLM4VPlugin.process_messages` expanded every `<video>` placeholder with the frame
count and the timestamps of the **first** video:

```python
num_frames = video_grid_thw[0][0] if len(video_grid_thw) > 0 else 0  # hard code for now
```

A sample with two videos of different lengths therefore got the first video's frame
count twice, while the visual tower still produced one entry per frame of *each*
video, so the prompt and the features disagree. `Qwen3VLPlugin` had the same line and
lost it in #10518; `GLM4VPlugin` kept it.

Measured on `zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking` with a 4-frame and an 8-frame video
(`video_grid_thw = [[2, 4, 4], [4, 4, 4]]`, so 2 + 4 = 6 frames are expected):

| | `<|begin_of_image|>` blocks | timestamps |
|---|---|---|
| before, transformers 4.55.0 | 4 | `0 1` / `0 1` |
| after | **6** | `0 1` / `0 1 2 3` |

The frame token budget now matches `sum(grid.prod() // merge_size ** 2)`, which is
what the model is going to hand back.

## The metadata contract

The same method could not run at all on transformers >= 4.57: the metadata still used
the pre-4.57 `VideoMetadata` field name and passed `images=None` to the video
processor.

```
TypeError: VideoMetadata.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'total_frames'
```

and it is included here because the multi-video fix is not reachable without it. One
thing #10538 does not cover: transformers >= 4.57 also dropped the `timestamps` key
that carried the frame timestamps, and answers with `video_metadata` instead. With
only the metadata change applied, on transformers 4.57.1 the crash is gone but every

items.bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Purpose

Integrate a new INT2 KV-cache quantisation backend.

Paper:**OSCAR** ([arXiv:2605.17757](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17757)). 
Code: https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/OSCAR 
(500+ stars, proved to be working on Qwen3-32B, GLM-4.7-FP8.)
Website: https://oscar-quantize.github.io/

vLLM already has TurboQuant, a data-free Hadamard-rotation KV-cache quantizer. Oscar is similar, but has better accuracy. If we apply the most aggresive quantisation method in TurboQuant, (`turboquant_3bit_nc`), the accuracy will drop by 20%. But with Oscar, for Qwen3-32B and GLM-4.7-FP8 respectively, the mean gap to BF16 is −0.02, and +0.27 points while reducing KV memory by ~8× and increasing large-batch throughput by up to ~7×. 

The main idea is, before applying clipped INT2 scalar quantization, we first apply a per-layer covariance-aware orthogonal rotation to distribute the values evenly, so they can be later de-quantised with higher precision. 

To use this feature, just need to load the original model checkpoints, and download a small per-layer rotation file
(`[head_dim, head_dim]` orthogonal matrices, a few MB), published in the [OSCAR RotationZoo](https://huggingface.co/Zhongzhu/OSCAR-RotationZoo).

## CC List
Paper author: @zzz0906
vLLM maintainer: @mgoin, @robertgshaw2-redhat 

## Implementation Details
- We stored rotation matrix for K and V. 
- Then, we use the same fp16 `(scale, zero)` parameter for each vector. We then store these values by re-using TurboQuant's `TQFullAttentionSpec` in a Combined `[key_packed | value_packed]` slot (72 B/token/kv-head

items.title: [RFC]: KVarN: a calibration-free, variance-normalized sub-8-bit KV-cache quantization backend
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

KV cache is the dominant memory cost for long-context and high-concurrency serving. vLLM already supports fp8 KV cache (~2x capacity) and, as of [#38479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38479), a sub-4-bit rotation-based backend (**TurboQuant**). But sub-4-bit KV quantization is still rarely turned on in production, for one reason: **it costs throughput and accuracy.**

As vLLM's own [TurboQuant blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-05-11-turboquant) reports, existing sub-4-bit methods buy 2.3 to 3.7x capacity but give up **40 to 52% of throughput**, and aggressive low-bit quant also tends to cost accuracy. Losing both speed and quality is why the feature stays off.

**KVarN** ([arXiv:2606.03458](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03458)) is a variance-normalized KV-cache quantization scheme built to keep all three at once: capacity, throughput, and accuracy.

- **~3.2 to 3.4x measured KV-cache capacity** at int4-K / int2-V.
- **Throughput at or above FP16/baseline in the memory-bound regime**, *uniquely* among KV-quant backends (measured +9% at 14B, rising to +18% at ~106B), not the throughput regression every other sub-4-bit method pays.
- **FP16-level accuracy**, calibration-free, no model changes, one flag (measured lossless on Qwen3-14B/30B and GLM-4.5-Air).

It also covers models TurboQuant cannot: it supports MLA, and it runs on hybrid and sliding-window models. TurboQuant supports full-attention and uniform sliding-window only.

Mechanism in one line: a Sinkhorn variance-normalizing rotation equalizes per-channel scale before scalar int4/int2 quantization, with a small fp16 outlier/sink pool, which is what preserves accuracy without calibration. (Full method in the paper.)

### Proposed Change.

Add KVarN as a **native vLLM attention backend selected via `--kv-cache-dtype`**, fully transparent (pass-through) for every non-KVarN dtype.

items.title: [Bug]: Native CPU offloading can compute inconsistent num_cpu_blocks across PP ranks
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Hardware: 4 × NVIDIA B300, single-node server
Architecture: x86_64
vLLM: 0.26.0 container for runtime reproduction; upstream main for the proposed fix
torch: 2.11.0+cu130
CUDA: 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.126.20
Distributed executor: mp, --pipeline-parallel-size 4, --tensor-parallel-size 1
KV offloading: native CPU offloading via OffloadingConnector, prefix caching enabled, no SSD offloading

Model
GLM-5.2-NVFP4

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Native CPU offloading can compute inconsistent CPU cache block counts across pipeline-parallel ranks.
A proposed fix is available in #50653

 ## Problem
In pipeline parallelism, each worker's `KVCacheConfig` only contains the layers owned by that worker's PP stage. Native CPU offloading derives its CPU cache capacity from the local worker KV cache tensors.

 When different PP stages own different numbers or types of layers, the per-worker KV bytes per block can differ. As a result, the scheduler and workers can compute different `num_cpu_blocks`.

The scheduler uses the first worker's KV cache config, while workers build offloading specs from their local configs. If the scheduler-side CPU block count is larger than a worker's local CPU buffer capacity, offloaded block IDs can exceed that worker's allocated CPU cache range.

 ## Example

 For a model with 8 layers, `pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=1`:

  ```text
  PP stage 0: 5 FullAttention layers
  PP stage 1: 3 FullAttention layers

  page_size_per_layer = 65536 bytes
  num_gpu_blocks = 1000
  cpu_bytes_to_use = 10 GiB
  ```
  Before the fix:
  ```text
  Scheduler / PP stage 0:
  total_gpu_kv_bytes = 5 * 65536 * 1000
  kv_bytes_per_block = 327680
  num_cpu_blocks = 32768

  Worker / PP stage 1:
  total_gpu_kv_bytes = 3 * 65536 * 1000
  kv_bytes_per_block = 196608
  num_cpu_blocks = 54613
  ```
 This means different PP ranks can allocate different CPU offload buffer sizes for the same scheduler-visible CPU block ID space.

## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

**At 1M-token prefill, LiteTopK accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash by 1.29× and 1.08×, respectively. LiteDSA increases the end-to-end speedups to 1.40× and 1.25×, with no accuracy loss.**

Fixes #46924. Supersedes #46925 (incomplete fix) and #46170 (`pop`→`get` only).

Tool schemas generated by Pydantic v2 use `$defs`/`$ref` to define nested types. Two bugs caused nested object arguments (e.g. `{"kind": "week"}`) to be double-encoded as JSON strings:

1. **No `$ref` resolution** — `find_tool_properties()` returned raw `$ref` pointers, and `extract_types_from_schema()` fell back to `["string"]` for unresolved references. This caused nested objects to be treated as strings.

2. **Destructive `pop("$defs")`** — `_get_tool_schema_defs()` used `params.pop("$defs", {})`, mutating the tool's parameter dict. On the streaming/engine path where `_get_tool_schema_defs` runs before `find_tool_properties`, the `$defs` were already gone, making ref resolution impossible even if added.

### Fix

- Add `_resolve_refs()` helper that inlines `$ref` pointers against `$defs` (Pydantic v2) and `definitions` (JSON Schema draft-07), with JSON Pointer escape decoding (`~0`→`~`, `~1`→`/`) and bounded recursion for cyclic schemas.
- Extract `_resolved_tool_properties()` to unify resolution for both definition namespaces.
- Update `find_tool_properties()` to resolve refs before returning — all downstream callers (qwen3_coder, deepseek_v32, seed_oss, glm4_moe, parser engine) automatically get concrete type information.
- Change `params.pop("$defs", {})` to `params.get("$defs", {})` in `_get_tool_schema_defs()` so definitions survive for subsequent argument coercion.

### Credit

This fix incorporates insights from:
- @hclsys who identified the `pop` ordering issue in #46925
- @alexeldeib who provided a complete supplementary patch with legacy defs support, cycle protection, and JSON Pointer decoding based on production traffic

The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A streaming tool call can end with `finish_reason` set while `arguments` is cut off mid-string. Any client that calls `json.loads` on the accumulated arguments fails on it. Reproduced live on Qwen3.8-27B in 7 of 25 requests sent straight at the worker, no proxy in the path.

`_safe_arg_prefix` (`parser_engine.py:299` on main at `8a2364605c0b`) deliberately streams unterminated string values for prefix-stable keys. Its own docstring (`:306-308`) carries the contract: "String values for keys in `string_keys` are prefix-stable, so stream their unterminated content instead of buffering long arguments until the closing tag arrives." Something has to close them, and that something is the flush.

`_flush_arg_converter` (`parser_engine.py:1052` on main) re-derives the arguments with `partial=False`. Four of the seven in-tree converters build their result from completed parameters and fold the still-open one in only under `if partial:`. So when generation ends while a parameter is open, the non-partial re-derivation **drops that parameter**, and the result is neither longer than nor a prefix of what was already streamed. Both guards (`:1068-1070`) fail, the function returns `None`, and nothing ever terminates the prefix the client is holding.

This is not conditional on the model misbehaving. Anything that ends generation with a parameter open reaches it: a `max_tokens` stop, a stop string, or a malformed continuation.

## Purpose

Adds an AITER-backed fusion path for the ROCm `deepseek_v32` (DeepSeek Sparse
Attention) forward, used by both DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2. The existing
shared-Triton fusion path is untouched and remains the default; the AITER path
is selected at runtime per fusion via opt-in env flags, so behaviour on ROCm is
unchanged unless a flag is set.

This PR is stacked on top of: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51915, so needs enablement to land first before this fusion add-on.

### Fusions added

**1. MLA dual RMSNorm** 
Fuses the q and kv-a RMSNorms into one AITER call
(`fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_out`). An out-variant was added so the norms write
model-owned buffers rather than allocating per layer, which lets the call be
hoisted out of the eager region and captured by cudagraph. Also wires the
per-token-quant variant for the quantized case.

**2. Fused QK RoPE + concat + MLA cache write** 
`rocm_aiter_fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` replaces the separate RoPE,
concat and KV-cache-write steps on the MLA path. The uint8 KV cache allocated by
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is viewed as `float8_e4m3fn` before the call, since the
AITER op rejects the raw uint8 buffer.

**3. Fused indexer QK RoPE + fp8 quant + cache write**
`rocm_aiter_indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` fuses the lightning-indexer key
LayerNorm, RoPE, fp8 quantization, and cache write into one call for the 21
indexer layers.

**4. Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm**
Uses AITER's custom all-reduce with an in-kernel RMSNorm. Gated on custom-AR
eligibility (`should_custom_ar`) because the op asserts the kernel ran, and
oversized batches must fall back to the standard path — this is the check the
torch.compile pass performs at compile time and which an inline call has to do
itself.

**5. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR`** exposes AITER's custom all-reduce
independently of the fused variant.

items.title: [Bugfix] Seed hybrid mamba state index with mamba_block_size on prefix-cache hits
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix an out-of-bounds read on prefix-cache hits for hybrid mamba models whose KV config contains a prefix-cacheable attention group with a block size smaller than `mamba_block_size` (e.g. a DFlash2/EAGLE sliding-window drafter group with block 64).

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`. By then `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has reassigned `cache_config.block_size = min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`, so on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA + sparse MLA, mamba block 7168, drafter block 64/1024) the seed is in the wrong units. `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` takes it as `src_col` and `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`): cached prefixes of ≥ 8 mamba blocks fault (`Xid 31`, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync), shorter hits silently restore the wrong recurrent state.

The fix divides by `cache_config.mamba_block_size`, the unit used for mamba blocks everywhere else (`MambaSpec.block_size`, the preprocess kernel, the block-table width; `mamba_attn.py` already derives the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`).

Fixes #55600.

## Test Plan

No unit test is included; the failure needs a hybrid model whose KV groups include a smaller-block prefix-cacheable group. Manual verification on GLM-5.3-Flash (EXL3, TP=1, DFlash2 `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `max_num_seqs=1`) on a DGX Spark, before/after on identical inputs.

## Test Result

- Prompt A = 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question: before → HTTP 500 in 0.2 s, `NVRM: Xid 31 ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`; after → completes in 11.7 s with 50 176 cached tokens.

items.title: kv-cache: honor scheduler lookahead in mamba align-mode allocation
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

In mamba align cache mode (mamba-hybrid models with prefix caching), `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` discarded all lookahead tokens by resetting `num_tokens` to `num_tokens_main_model`. When the scheduler schedules lookahead capacity beyond a main-model sequence that ends exactly on a page boundary, this corrupts the recurrent state in two ways.

## Root cause

A mamba state table row is page-indexed: the worker's running-state column is `cdiv(main_end, bs) - 1`.

1. **Missing next page.** When a chunk ends exactly on a page boundary and lookahead tokens extend beyond it, the next page was not materialized with the current schedule. The boundary token's state write then targeted a block-table entry that still held a recycled stale block — the recurrent state is corrupted from that point on (one-step NaN followed by a repetition lock at every page boundary).

2. **Displaced running-state column.** If a page was materialized for the lookahead, the null padding was derived from the inflated `num_tokens`, so the reserved page displaced the real running-state column. The worker's running-state index (0 for a chunk ending at the first page boundary) pointed at the null slot; the next chunk's state pre-copy chained from the null slot and spec-decode acceptance collapsed to zero permanently for that request.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced on a 4-node Arm (Thor SM110) cluster serving GLM-5.3-Flash (mamba-hybrid + MTP + prefix caching) with deterministic single-turn probes: prompts whose prefill chunk ends exactly on a page boundary produced 0% spec-decode acceptance from the first decode step, while boundary-crossing-free prompts were healthy. The failure moved with cache layout across boots, and per-request scheduler dumps of the mamba state-table rows showed the displaced null column exactly at the worker's running-state index. The corruption was confirmed to chain through the state pre-copy (pre-copy source = the null slot).

## Purpose

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087. GLM-5.3 KDA merges the q/k/v short-conv weights into one cached tensor (`_merged_conv_weight`), built lazily on first forward. Online-RL workflows warm up with dummy weights (cache built), then refit `q_conv1d`/`k_conv1d`/`v_conv1d` — but the cached merge is never invalidated, so inference silently keeps using the pre-refit convolution weights.

## Approach

Weight loading dispatches on the param's stamped `weight_loader` (`getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` in `AutoWeightsLoader`). So the cache can be invalidated at exactly the point the weights change: in `Glm5NextLinearAttention.__init__`, wrap each conv weight's stamped loader so any write clears `_merged_conv_weight`. The next forward rebuilds it from the current params. No new hooks, no changes to the reload machinery.

## Coverage / limitations

- ✅ Initial load (loaders run before first forward; cache built after anyway)
- ✅ Checkpoint-format refit: `reload_weights` → `model.load_weights` → stamped loaders → cache cleared
- ✅ Layerwise reload: re-dispatches through the same stamped loaders

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55569. Related: #56457 reports the same allocation pattern in the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer, with fixes proposed for that path in #56500 and #57105 (both open); #55572 (closed) lowered the default logits budget on integrated GPUs instead.

The dense sparse-MLA indexer (`sparse_attn_indexer.py`, and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool variant under `models/glm5next`) scores each prefill chunk with DeepGEMM's `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`, which allocates its `[M, N]` fp32 logits inside the C++ API. `N` is the request's compressed context so far, so every chunk of a long prefill asks for a tensor of a new, larger size: one launch per chunk of growing size while `M * N * 4` fits the `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` budget (512 MiB), and, once a chunk exceeds it (about 116k tokens at a 4,608-token chunk with kpool 4), several launches per chunk that are all close to the budget but never the same size twice. PyTorch's caching allocator serves a request from a cached block only if it fits, and returns segments to the driver only on `empty_cache` or an OOM-time release, so once the free space that happens to be around is used up, each chunk step adds a new segment for the rest of the prefill. items.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM90 sparse MLA IMA on >16k-row steps by chunking plan/run
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a CUDA illegal-memory-access crash whenever a single scheduled step packs more than 16384 query rows on the SM90 sparse MLA backend (the GLM-5.3-Flash default), e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` with a 28k-token prefill chunk, or 32k tokens scheduled across concurrent requests.

**Root cause (flashinfer 0.6.18.post1, the pinned version).** The SM90 batch-MLA plan hardcodes `max_total_num_works = 16384` and never checks it: the load-balancing schedule is `std::copy`'d into per-array regions sized for 16384 works, so a larger step silently overwrites neighboring schedule arrays, and the kernel then reads garbage `q_indptr`/`kv_indptr` (IMA in `BatchMLAPageAttentionHopper`). This backend feeds one varlen row per query token, so any step with more than 16384 scheduled tokens overflows. flashinfer 0.7.0 raised the limit to 65536 and added a hard error, but vLLM pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`. Small overflows (e.g. 16385 works) do not even fault — they run with a corrupted schedule.

**Fix.** When a step has more than `_MAX_PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS = 8192` query rows, plan and run the MQA as independent row chunks: the builder plans each chunk into its own `_SM90State` (a lazily grown pool), and `forward_mqa` runs each state's row range and concatenates. Each row is already an independent varlen query (causality is encoded in the top-k selection, `causal=False`), so chunking is exact. The bound is 8192 rather than 16384 so the work count stays provably under 16384 even with split-kv rows: works <= rows + total_kv_len / kv_len_limit, and `kv_len_limit` tracks total_kv_len / num_clusters. Steps at or under the limit keep the existing single-plan path unchanged, including CUDA-graph replay.

## Not a duplicate

- #56969 fixed a different OOB in this backend (mixed prefill/decode batches); it is in the tested tree and the crash still reproduces without this change.
- #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and the indexer prefill workspace sizing; different call sites.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

A DEP32 GLM-5.3 prefill group (4 pods x 8 DP ranks, DeepEP) dies as a unit: one rank stops between steps, the other 31 wait for it in `internode_dispatch`, hit the 100 s DeepEP timeout and trap (Xid 43); the stalled rank never traps. Captured on a production group right after its first real requests:

- The stalled worker's main thread was in kernel state `D` inside `__vm_munmap` for 73 s, ran for 1 s, then in a 16 KiB anonymous `mmap` (`vm_mmap_pgoff`) for 88 s. `py-spy` could not attach for exactly that window, since it needs `mmap_lock` as well.
- `perf` on the same workers under load: 1,000-3,400 `mmap` + `munmap` calls per second per worker, all 16 KiB. CPython 3.12 allocates a new frame data-stack chunk with `mmap` when a call crosses the end of the current chunk and frees it on return (python/cpython#142183, fixed in 3.13.13); the MoE forward crosses that boundary in every layer.
- The node sat at its free-memory floor for the whole stall: MemFree 16 GiB against MemAvailable 896 GiB (about 700 GiB of clean checkpoint pages plus a 761 GiB CPU KV tier in shm), with direct-reclaim bursts (`pgscan_direct` 7k-20k per 5 s), `compact_stall` 23-56 per 5 s and hundreds of `thp_fault_fallback`. MemFree jumped from 17 to 344 GiB the moment the group died.

`mmap` and `munmap` take the process `mmap_lock` for write; a page fault takes it for read and, with no free pages, holds it through direct reclaim and compaction. ## Purpose

Fix two independent ways an image request takes down the engine in the GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower.

**1. ## Purpose

Enable prefill context parallelism (hybrid PCP) for GLM-5.3's KDA linear-attention layers with KCP, a two-pass parallel scan over each rank's zig-zag prefill segments on FlashKDA kernels:

1. Prepare every local segment once with FlashKDA's preparation kernel.
2. Summarize each segment as an affine map from that workspace: one FlashKDA-derived recurrence over the value columns from a zero state (S) plus the identity's columns with zero input (the transition M). Like FlashKDA's K2 after vllm-project/FlashKDA#13, it keeps the state in FP32 between tiles. items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

On ROCm native decode is used for `next_n` 1 and 2 today, so MTP with on

items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reject cudagraph_mode=FULL at startup
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse cannot capture prefill or mixed batches in CUDA graphs. It picks its prefill path from per-step page residency (resident pages, or spilled pages staged from host), and it mirrors prefill KV to host outside the graph. With `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a backend reporting `ALWAYS` support (FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100) has prefill/mixed batches captured as FULL graphs. A replay could then take the branch frozen at capture and skip the host mirror.

## Changes

HiSparse rejects `cudagraph_mode=FULL` at config validation, next to its other unsupported-config checks (PP, DCP). The error points to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (the default), which keeps FULL graphs for decode batches. Being a config check, it covers every backend HiSparse runs on.

Separately, `FULL` with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100 currently crashes on prefill replay even without HiSparse: #59681.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_rejects_full_cudagraph_mode` in `tests/test_config.py`.
- B200, shrunk GLM-5.3 (dummy weights), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a small pool so prefill context spills to host: TRTLLM ragged and FlashAttention prefill.

## Test Result

- The new test fails without the change; `tests/test_config.py -k hisparse`: 13 passed.
- B200, before: `FULL` + HiSparse crashed in both runs: a mixed active/empty query rows error with TRTLLM ragged prefill, an illegal memory access with FlashAttention prefill. Now it fails at startup with the error above.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step.

The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path.

## Claims

- Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
- No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Build tool-call grammars from the tools the prompt renders
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Non-Harmony chat templates only render function tools. Responses namespace functions are flattened to `<namespace>__<name>`, and builtin tools (`mcp`, `web_search`, ...) are dropped (`construct_tool_dicts`). The tool-call structural tag was built from every request tool instead, so the grammar and the prompt disagreed:

- **Builtin-only tools:** they produce no grammar rule, so the tag is empty and xgrammar rejects it. Since #56403 this returns `400` for every GLM-4.7 Responses request whose tools are all builtin. PLaMo3, MiMo and HY-V4 fail the same way, and so does any model with `tool_choice="required"` (an opaque `400`, or a bare `AssertionError` inside xgrammar).
- **Namespace functions:** the model is shown them but has no grammar rule for them. Under a constrained grammar it is blocked from calling them, or forced into a different tool. The legacy JSON-schema path, used when strict tool calling is off, silently returned an empty `completed` response for `required` with only builtin tools.

The first commit fixed the GLM-4.7 builder only. This change fixes it at the shared entry point:

- `get_function_tools()` (`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py`) is the single source of the tools the model is shown. The prompt helpers, `get_structural_tag_tools()` in the structural tag registry, and the legacy JSON-schema `required` path are all built from it, so the prompt and the grammar cannot drift apart.

## Overview

The SM121 `(10240, 320)` skinny-GEMM plan for the Qwen4Exp HC up projection never runs. items.title: [Perf][HiSparse] Cache per-request residency instead of rescanning every page each step
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse decode is CPU-bound on main because of one scheduler-side scan. Every step, `HiSparseCoordinator.all_context_pages_resident` walks every page of every scheduled request in every resident group (one group per layer), only to decide whether prefill can skip host staging. That is O(requests × context pages × layers) Python per step, even for pure-decode batches.

The scan arrived in c4b9b7deac ("bypass host resolution for resident decode"), after the GLM-5.3 results in #53781 were measured, and shipped with 3/N. This PR caches the requests whose resident pages are all non-null. A request is scanned once. Pages become null only at admission or host import, before the first scan, or when the pool reuses an unpinned page (`_lose_page`), so those paths plus `free` drop the cache entry. The per-step check is O(requests).

HiSparse-only change (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this scan.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead on the GPU and in launches:

- **One slot-invalidation launch per step.** Today it's one eager launch per leader layer after the forward graph (61 for DeepSeek-V3.2). The kernel now runs over (written tokens × index groups) using a cached device table of each group's `device_global_indices`. `HiSparseRuntime.invalidate_written_slots` is replaced by `HiSparseSlotInvalidator`.

items.title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Size per-region replicate flags by each region's block count
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Background

With P_TP > D_TP (e.g. PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode), each decoder rank reads a block from several prefill ranks. Each local descriptor gets a replicate flag: full-attention regions are **SPLIT** (each rank fills its head slice), MLA regions are **REPLICATE** (whole block read once).

`_fa_desc_replicated` assumed every region holds the same number of blocks. HiSparse breaks this: host-resident MLA regions hold `hisparse_host_num_blocks`, GPU regions hold `num_blocks`. Every P_TP > D_TP handshake into a HiSparse decoder failed with `AssertionError: FA desc flags N != num_fa_descs M`.

## Fix

Build the flags the same way `_build_fa_local` builds the descriptors: same region order, `region_num_blocks[i] * block_size_ratio` per region. Companion fix for the same topology: #60108. No other open PR touches this function.

## Validation

**main vs. this PR**, checked against the descriptors `_build_fa_local` emits:

| Region layout | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Equal block counts | OK | OK |
| HiSparse, unequal block counts | assert | OK |
| Unequal counts that divide evenly | flags silently wrong | OK |
| Layer-name routing, region listed twice | flags silently wrong | OK |

**E2E** (GLM-5.3, 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 HiSparse decode, with #60108): main asserts on the first request. items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Carry adopted prefix pages in the new request's row
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109: HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access when a new request hits a prefix whose published host pages still have GPU copies.

The coordinator adopts those copies after the scheduler has already built the request's `NewRequestData`, so the adopted row went out as a `block_table_updates` entry. For a new request, model runner V2 then stages two full-row writes for the same row in one step (`add_requests`, then `update_requests`), and the staged-write kernel applies them in parallel with no ordering. A rank that kept the pre-adoption row saw null resident pages, while the scheduler reported every context page resident. The resident-prefill shortcut then sent the prefill rows through the decode residency resolver, whose host union overflowed `max_union_rows` and faulted.

The fix puts the adopted row in the new request's `block_ids`; `block_table_updates` stays for running requests. HiSparse-only (`hisparse/connector.py`).

Note: MRv2's staged block-table writer doesn't order overlapping writes to the same row. This PR stops HiSparse from producing them; changing that in core is a separate discussion.

## Reproduction on main

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, either TP8 or TP4 (`host_pool_gib` 128 or 64):

```bash

items.title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Write a new request's block-table update once
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109 at the consumer; alternative to #60117, which fixes the HiSparse producer.

`SchedulerOutput.block_table_updates` carries authoritative rows that supersede a request's normal block-table writes. `update_requests` already honors that for running requests (`req_id not in table_updates`), but not for requests added in the same step. For those, MRv2 stages two full-row writes to one row: `add_requests` writes `NewRequestData.block_ids`, then `update_requests` writes the update. `_apply_write_kernel` applies a step's staged writes as independent programs with no ordering, so each rank can end up with either row.

HiSparse is currently the only producer. When a new request's host prefix hit adopts surviving GPU copies, some ranks kept the pre-adoption row with null resident pages, and the decode residency resolver overflowed and faulted (illegal memory access).

The fix: `add_requests` writes the update's row for a new request, and `update_requests` skips updates for requests added this step. Each row gets one staged write per step. The new-request id set is built only when there are table updates, so steps without updates do no extra work.

## Why core rather than #60117

#60117 avoids the race by moving the update into `NewRequestData` inside the HiSparse connector. That fixes today's only producer, but leaves MRv2 accepting two unordered writes to one row from any future producer. This PR applies the existing "update supersedes" rule uniformly where the race happens. It's a 13-line change in `gpu/model_runner.py`; the staged writer is untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] New `test_new_request_table_update_is_written_once` (`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`). It fails on main (`append_block_ids` called twice) and passes with the fix; the file's 9 tests pass. Run: `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`.
